articles.title: A Black Figure Skater Just Made History. Here’s Why It Matters
articles.summary: Last weekend, American figure skater Alexa Gasparotto made history as the first Black woman ever to land a triple axel at the International Skating Union Grand Prix. This jump is symbolic of something far larger. While Black competitors in Olympic figure skating are still few and far between, we exist vibrantly. Gasparotto’s triple axel was a byproduct of a long effort in a small, expensive sport for more visibility and support for skaters of all marginalized backgrounds. articles.title: What Comes Next After Historic Myanmar Genocide Ruling
articles.summary: The world’s top international court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority, more than a million of whom remain displaced. The verdict , issued Thursday, is the first time a state has been found responsible for committing genocide in the history of the International Court of Justice, which was established in 1945. articles.title: What Does It Mean to Age Well? Three Experts Weigh In
articles.summary: When people tell Dr. Dean Ornish they want to live longer, he asks them why. Maybe they want to dance at their kid’s wedding, they say, or finally write the book they’ve been thinking about for years. Whatever their answer, it gives them something to work toward and can make changing a habit today feel worth the effort.
